post.description:
Add environments (the wizard's third step): their roots and settings, and the folders never to
index. Nothing is read from them until they are scanned (``/jobs/rescan`` with the ids).

Change an environment's settings: the fields given replace the ones it has (``exchange env
config``). Ignore rules apply from the next rescan.

get.description:
Every process package: trusted or not, its prerequisites (green or red with how to fix them),
its options, and what trusting it allows. Only ready ones are offered for requisitions.

post.description: Trust a package as it is now: it may then run its own code. Ask the user first.
Copy a package folder into the user's processes folder; it stays untrusted until trusted.

get.description: Where the user said external tools are (Blender, texconv, Daz Studio...).

schema.title: Response Get Tools Api V1 Tools Get

post.description: Set a tool's path (null forgets it: manifests' likely paths are tried again).

schema.title: Response Set Tool Path Api V1 Tools Post

get.description: Saved option sets: those shipped in packages, then the user's.

schema.title: Response List Presets Api V1 Presets Get

post.description: Save options (by process) under a name; a user preset of that name is replaced.

schema.title: Response Remove Preset Api V1 Presets  Name  Delete

get.description: The options last queued with each process.

schema.title: Response Get Last Used Api V1 Presets Last Used Get

get.description:
Where requisitions write in each environment (Settings › Endpoints): the folder, whether
the user chose it, and its visibility. Change them with ``/environments/{id}/config``.

schema.title: Response List Endpoints Api V1 Endpoints Get

post.description:
The chains of processes that take these assets (and products' children) into an
environment: the dialog's route list (besides Automatic).

schema.title: Response Route Choices Api V1 Requisitions Routes Post

post.description:
Plan getting assets into an environment (nothing is written): per asset, the items (a
product's children too), each with its process chain, source and problems; the option forms
for the processes in it; and warnings.

Plan this request again and queue every plan with something included; the options become
each process's last used. Run them with ``/jobs/requisitions``.

get.description: The queue (waiting or running, in order), then finished requisitions, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Requisitions Api V1 Requisitions Get

get.description: One requisition: its items (with outputs) and every file it wrote.

post.description: Keep a queued requisition from running (``held`` false lets it run again).
Put a waiting requisition at a place in the queue (1 is first).

Queue it again after a checkpoint or a collision (with how to settle collisions); failed
items are retried. Run the queue to continue.

Queue a fulfilled or stale requisition again with the current processes, overwriting its
output; returns the new requisition.
Mark fulfilled requisitions whose sources or processes changed as stale; the ones newly found.

schema.title: Response Check Stale Api V1 Requisitions Check Stale Post

post.description: Run the queue (or some requisitions) in a worker process (``exchange requisition run``).

Move what a requisition wrote to the recycle folder and put back what it overwrote, then
rescan the folders it wrote to (``exchange requisition remove``).
The claim these fields would make, with its path and whose turn it is. Writes nothing.
Make the claim: a file in the claims folder. Returns it as ``GET /claims/{id}`` does.

get.description: Claims newest first, and a line for each file that could not be read (never filtered).
